practicesLabel: Inquiry, Chemistry Command Terms and HL Extensions
practices: Assessments evaluate Structure and Reactivity core plus all HL Extensions. High emphasis on analytical quantitative calculations, stereochemistry, and organic reaction mechanisms. Strict adherence to command terms. Calculations require rigorous numerical proofs.

keyTopics: Particulate nature of matter and physical changes
The nuclear atom, isotopes, nuclear symbols
Electron configurations, subshells (s, p, d) and transition metals (HL Extension)
Counting particles by mass: The mole, molar mass

units.unitTitle: Models of bonding and structure (SL + HL)
keyTopics: The ionic model, crystal lattices, formula units
The covalent model, Lewis structures, coordinate bonds, hybridisation, sigma and pi bonds (HL Extension)
Macromolecules (silicon dioxide, diamond) and metallic bonding
From models to real substances, electronegativity differences
Measuring energy changes in chemical reactions, calorimetry
Enthalpy changes, combustion, neutralization, Hess's Law
Entropy (S) and thermodynamic spontaneity (Gibbs, G) (HL Extension)
Born-Haber energy cycles and lattice enthalpies (HL Extension)

units.unitTitle: How much, how fast and how far? (SL + HL)
keyTopics: Rate laws, concentration-time graphs, and reaction mechanisms (HL Extension)
Equilibrium law, Kc and Kp calculations
Proton transfer reactions, strong acids, weak acids and buffer calculations (HL Extension)
Electron transfer reactions, redox cells, electrolysis, Nernst equations (HL Extension)
Organic Chemistry: Functional groups, nomenclature, Sn1/Sn2/elimination mechanisms (HL Extension)

antiPatterns: Ensure students show advanced orbital and thermodynamic reasoning. Out of scope are: memorization of specific enzyme name lists beyond core models; complete listing of industrial manufacture designs (keep to general equilibrium application); and complex organic pathways not specified in the 2025 syllabus.
